chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:
Concerning a man who struck another man in his ear with a bone, and he claimed that he could not hear, he said:

“He is to be watched, tested unawares, and waited upon for a year. Then if he hears, or if two men testify against him that he heard, otherwise he is to be made to swear an oath and he is to be given the diyah.”
It was said: O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, what if it is discovered afterward that he heard? He said: “If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, restored his hearing to him, then I do not hold anything against him.”

key_terms.أُذُنِهِ: his ear, the injured body part under legal consideration
key_terms.حَلَّفَهُ: he is made to swear an oath to support his claim
key_terms.رَجُلَانِ: two men, the number of witnesses required here for testimony
key_terms.سَمْعَهُ: his hearing, the faculty alleged to have been lost and possibly restored
key_terms.لَا يَسْمَعُ: does not hear, the claimed disability
key_terms.يُتَرَصَّدُ: he is watched or monitored to verify the claim
key_terms.يُسْتَغْفَلُ: he is tested unawares to determine whether he can hear

ai.seo_question: How is a claim of hearing loss from an injury verified in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a claim of hearing loss caused by injury. The claimant is to be observed and tested over time, and if the loss cannot be disproven, he may confirm his claim by oath and receive the diyah. If his hearing later returns by the act of Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ, no liability is held against him for the earlier ruling.
